title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US stocks fell Tuesday for a second straight session (Dow -0.3%, Nasdaq -0.1%) as the 10-year Treasury yield hit a fresh 19-year high and the 30-year hit its highest since 2002, while consumer confidence dropped to a 12-year low.

Markets: Brent crude fell 2.6% to ~$102.59/bbl as Mideast oil flows showed signs of easing; bitcoin is on pace for its best quarter since Q4 2024 (+40% since July), and the dollar has gained 1.5% this month on rising yields.

Companies: AMD is paying over $8B to acquire Fei-Fei Li's World Labs, with Li joining as chief scientist; Anthropic's leaked IPO prospectus shows a $42B 2025 net loss, revenue up 12x to ~$4.6B, and a target valuation above $2T.

Companies: OpenAI scrapped its next flagship model release over safety concerns ahead of today's DevDay; Florida's AG is seeking a court injunction to halt ChatGPT development, and SpaceX's next-gen Starship test ended in an explosion after returning early.

Macro/Policy: NY Fed's John Williams said the Fed need not rush its next rate increase, signaling a possible pause until December and pushing back on market bets for a near-term hike (Fed funds stands at 3.75-4.0% after September's hike).

Macro/Policy: Trump, Vance and AI CEOs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Palantir) gather today for an AI "Golden Age" event amid bipartisan unease over AI safety incidents; Wednesday brings ADP employment, PCE inflation and Q2 GDP data, plus Micron, Conagra and Levi Strauss earnings.
